**Analysis:**

- **Affected part**: Stem/crown region — stem split open longitudinally near soil line
- **Key features**:
  - White mycelial growth on the exterior of the stem at the soil/crown interface
  - Stem cut open showing yellowed/bleached internal tissue
  - Plant completely wilted and dead — leaves brown and desiccated
  - Sandy, dry soil (characteristic habitat)
  - Roots visible and affected

**Reasoning through classes:**

- **Southern Blight** (Sclerotium rolfsii): Classic white mycelial fan/mat on stem at soil line, rapid plant death, thrives in hot sandy soils — matches well
- **Sclerotinia Timber Rot**: Also white mycelium, but typically produces large black sclerotia inside hollow bleached stem, and affects stem at multiple heights
- **Verticillium Wilt / Bacterial Wilt**: No white mycelium; vascular discoloration is internal only
- **Southern Bacterial Wilt**: Bacterial — no visible mycelium

The white fungal mat on the stem base at the soil line in sandy, dry conditions is the hallmark of **Southern Blight**. The plant shows complete collapse consistent with crown rot from *Sclerotium rolfsii*.
